attributes.body_ja:
「てご覧（らん）」は、「なさい」と同（おな）じように使（つか）われる、丁寧（ていねい）な表現（ひょうげん）です。主（おも）に「どうぞ (A) をやってみて」のような意味（いみ）で使（つか）われます。(A) は動詞（どうし）のテ形（けい）で、そのあとに「ご覧（らん）」を付（つ）けます。

「てご覧（らん）」の「覧（らん）」は、もともと「よく見（み）ること」や「広（ひろ）く眺（なが）めること」を意味（いみ）する漢字（かんじ）です。「てごらん」は「てみる」と使（つか）われる場面（ばめん）が似（に）ていますが、「てごらん」の方（ほう）がより優（やさ）しく丁寧（ていねい）な言（い）い方（かた）です。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

名詞（めいし）の「ご覧（らん）」は尊敬語（そんけいご）なので、話（はな）し手（て）自身（じしん）の行動（こうどう）には使（つか）えません。ほかの人（ひと）に「やってみて」と勧（すす）めるときにだけ使（つか）えます。

注意点（ちゅういてん）

「ごらん」と「なさい」が合（あ）わさって、「ごらんなさい」の形（かたち）で使（つか）われるときもあります。この場合（ばあい）、表現（ひょうげん）の強（つよ）さが少（すこ）し増（ま）し、命令（めいれい）のように聞（き）こえるので、目上（めうえ）・年上（としうえ）の人（ひと）が、目下（めした）・年下（としした）の人（ひと）に「やってみなさい」と言（い）うときによく使（つか）われます。
attributes.body:
てご覧（らん） is an honorific language expression in Japanese that is used in a similar way to なさい. It is usually translated as 'please try to (A)', where (A) is the verb that ご覧（らん） is connected to, through the use of the conjunction particle て.

However, despite being translated as 'please try to (A)', the literal meaning of 覧（らん） is 'to look', or 'to peruse' (to look at one's own leisure, without needing to rush). Due to this, てごらん can be thought of as being quite similar to てみる 'to try', but with the added emphasis of 'try as you like, when it suits you'.

Caution

As ご覧（らん） is honorific language, it cannot be used to refer to your own actions, or things that you will 'try'. It will only ever be used to make suggestions to other people about what they should try.

Caution

Sometimes ごらん and なさい will be paired together. This slightly increases the strength of the suggestion, and may be perceived as a very light command. Because of this, ごらんなさい is primarily used by superiors/elders, when requesting that a subordinate/younger person try something.

attributes.source: [AIAIJ] An Integrated Approach to Intermediate Japanese

attributes.description: ちょうだい、ごらん、てください、おいで

attributes.body: てください is a basic way to express a polite request ('Please do…'). For example, 食べてください would mean 'Please eat (this).' It is polite and neutral, and can be used with strangers or people equal in status to you. てごらん is a gentle request form often used by adults to children, etc., that adds a nuance of 'Give this a try' or 'Try doing this (to see how you like it).'

ないでください is a polite way to ask someone not to do something. It's neutral and appropriate for strangers or people of equal status. In contrast, てごらん is a gentle request form often used by adults to children, etc., that adds a nuance of 'Give this a try' or 'Try doing this (to see how you like it).'

てみる expresses trying something to see what it's like, similar to the English 'try (doing)', e.g. 食べてみる ('I'll try eating it.'). てごらん is a more directive form that encourages someone else to try something, e.g. 食べてごらん ('Try eating it.' as a gentle request). てごらん is often used by adults to children, or superiors to subordinates. Among peers, something like 食べてみて would be more common.

Both are command forms, but with different tones. なさい is a polite but direct command, often used by teachers or parents, e.g. 食べなさい ('Eat.'). てごらん is softer and gently encourages someone to give something a try, e.g. 食べてごらん ('Try eating it'). Both are typically used from adults to children, or superiors to subordinates.

The dictionary/non-past form of a verb + な expresses a blunt command not to do something. In contrast, てごらん is a gentle encouragement to try doing something. For example, 食べるな！ means 'Don't eat it!' while 食べてごらん means 'Try eating it' Both are used toward someone of lower status, such as an adult speaking to a child.
